step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Nike's social graph processing system powered by Amazon Neptune. The workflow starts with the Nike App (UserConsumerMobile) sending user preferences to Amazon API Gateway. API Gateway passes the request to AWS Lambda, which siphons the data and routes it down to an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB). The ELB distributes traffic to an EC2 Auto Scaling group, where the application business logic executes. The Auto Scaling group performs writes to the Amazon Neptune database cluster (1 writer, 2 reader nodes) using an A-R-B relationship model. Simultaneously, the Auto Scaling instances publish notification events to Amazon SNS, which fans out messages to two downstream subscribers: CDS (Nike's internal notification system) and the Data Lake.

graph.name: Nike Social Graph Architecture with Amazon Neptune
graph.notes: Nike powers its social graph across mobile apps (Nike, NRC, NTC) using Amazon Neptune for personalization, managing 125 million user relationships for roughly 25 million users globally.

nodes.name: NIKE APP
nodes.notes: Mobile application where users onboard and select interest preferences (e.g., sports like basketball or tennis).

nodes.name: API GATEWAY
nodes.notes: Entry point intake funnel for receiving user preference data from the Nike App.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Siphons incoming preference data from API Gateway without complex business logic.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer ensuring high availability and global resiliency for inbound traffic.

nodes.name: AUTO SCALING
nodes.notes: Auto-scaled EC2 instances executing core application business logic, graph writes, and event publishing.

nodes.name: NEPTUNE
nodes.notes: Amazon Neptune graph database cluster (1 writer node, 2 reader nodes) storing A-R-B entity relationships.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Amazon SNS topic used to broadcast user preference updates to multiple internal subscribers asynchronously.

nodes.name: CDS
nodes.notes: Nike internal notification system acting upon user preference signals to deliver personalized content.

nodes.name: DATA LAKE
nodes.notes: Data lake repository consuming user interest events for analytics and personalization modeling.

edges.notes: User interest selection payload sent from Nike App to API Gateway.
API Gateway routes request to Lambda siphon function.
Lambda forwards preference payload to ELB.
ELB load balances traffic across Auto Scaling EC2 instances.
Auto Scaling EC2 instances execute synchronous/asynchronous writes to the Neptune cluster.
Auto Scaling instances trigger an event message to SNS upon user graph updates.
SNS notifies CDS internal notification system.
SNS notifies Data Lake for downstream analytics processing.
